sections.h2: Which Buncombe County offices deal with my tax bill?
sections.html:
One department, Tax Assessment, covers the whole cycle from its building at 182 College Street in Asheville. The doors are open weekdays between 8 am and 5 pm. Listing, appraising and assessing belong to the assessor, and billing and collecting belong to the collector.

Each desk has its own number, so dial the one that matches your question.

  • Real estate values and appeal forms: 828-250-4940
  • Payments, balances and payment plans: 828-250-4910
  • Senior, disability and veteran relief: 828-250-4915
  • Business and personal property: 828-250-4930
  • Land records: 828-250-4970

You can also type an address into tax.buncombenc.gov to see the property record card, the bill and the appeal request. Anyone preparing to sell a Buncombe house should ask the collections desk for the balance on the parcel before choosing a closing date.

sections.h2: Why do 2026 Buncombe tax bills use 2021 values?
sections.html:
Because of a law the General Assembly passed in July 2026, the county must hold off on its new values until January 1, 2027. Bills for 2026 therefore rest on the schedule from the 2021 reappraisal, even though the county had finished a reappraisal as of January 1, 2026 and mailed owners their new numbers.

Two measures were involved: S.B. 889 (S.L. 2026-8), which delayed the schedule for a short list of counties that includes Buncombe, and S.B. 474 (S.L. 2026-47), which offered a way out through a revenue-neutral rate. The county said that rate would round to 40 cents. At a July 14, 2026 special meeting, commissioners picked the old values and a higher rate so the budget approved on June 2, 2026 would stand.

For most owners nothing moved. Unless you built or altered something, the value matches last year's, and last year's value already carried any Tropical Storm Helene adjustment. Mailed bills ran late, with most residential bills posted online first.

sections.h2: What rates appear on a 2026 Buncombe County bill?
sections.html:
The county levy is 61.54 cents on each $100 of value, and the districts below add their own. Your parcel's address decides which of them apply.

Rates the county adopted on July 14, 2026
Taxing unitCents per $100 of valueSource
Buncombe County61.54County news release of July 14, 2026
Unified Fire District17.38County news release of July 14, 2026
Asheville City Schools11.75County news release of July 14, 2026

Because the county assigns values for every town and district inside it, the delay reached those units too. The 40-cent option reached only the county's own rate. City and town rates come from their own governing boards, so read the lines on your bill.

sections.h2: What are the payment dates and options in Buncombe County?
sections.html:
A bill is normally due September 1, and the county lets owners pay through the following January 5 without a penalty. For the 2026 bills, that final penalty-free day is January 5, 2027.

After that, state law adds 2% interest from January 6 until February 1, then three quarters of one percent for each month or part of a month. A mailed payment counts as paid on its postmark date.

Owners who need more time can ask Tax Collections for a plan, either a Casual Payment Plan or a Preauthorized Debit Payment Plan. While you stay enrolled, the county does not use garnishments of wages or bank accounts. Call 828-250-4910 and ask for a collection specialist.

sections.h2: How can I contest my Buncombe County property value?
sections.html:
Two routes exist: an informal review by Property Assessment, or a formal hearing before the Board of Equalization and Review. The county's August 2026 guidance said an appeal of the value on the current bill could be filed through December 31, 2026.

To start online, enter your address at tax.buncombenc.gov, pick View Parcel, then Tax Appeal Request. A mailed form is available from 828-250-4940. Over 16,000 appeals came in on the 2026 reappraisal values, and the county is holding the unresolved ones for the 2027 reappraisal, so nobody has to refile unless a decision came back and they disagree.

  • Under G.S. 105-322 the board may lower, raise or confirm a value after hearing evidence.
  • Ask for the hearing before the board adjourns; a decision notice mailed late gives you 15 days from its mailing.
  • The board mails its ruling within a month of adjourning.
  • Beyond that, notify the Property Tax Commission in writing within 30 days of the mailed ruling.

sections.h2: Who gets relief on a Buncombe County bill?
sections.html:
The county runs the three programs that state law creates, and the application window is January 1 through June 1. A household can use only one program at a time.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: shields the larger of $25,000 or half of the home's appraised value, for owners aged 65 and up or totally and permanently disabled, with income at or below the cap. The cap printed for 2026 is $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: removes the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: holds tax to 4% of income, or 5% when income runs above the cap up to $58,200 for 2026. The excess is deferred and becomes a lien, due if the owner sells or leaves.

The county has also cautioned that online videos describe a federal senior property tax exemption that does not exist, and it asks older owners to use only its official applications. Separately, its General Assistance Program, described at buncombenc.gov/gap, offers short-term help with housing and utility costs.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Buncombe County tax when I sell?
sections.html:
The debt attaches to the parcel, so it gets settled from the proceeds at or before closing. State law makes the lien attach as of the date property is listed each year, and penalties, interest and costs ride along. The county may enforce it through a foreclosure suit filed where the land sits.

Call Tax Collections at 828-250-4910 for the figure before fixing a closing date. If you hold a circuit breaker deferral, expect that balance to come due on the sale. A buyer's attorney will also want proof that the account is paid before the deed goes to the register of deeds at 205 College Street.

Owners with an open appeal should keep the paperwork handy, since the outcome applies to the 2027 value that the next buyer will see.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers tell me about Buncombe County homeowners?
sections.html:
Buncombe's July 2025 estimate was 277,417 people in 142,799 housing units spread across 656.50 square miles of land. The median owner-occupied home is $391,800, and 66.2% of homes are owned.

Median household income is $74,436. Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,785 a month, owners without one pay $505, and renters pay a median $1,362 in gross rent. The Census Bureau shows 12.4% of residents in poverty and 23.2% aged 65 or older, an age group that includes many people eligible for state relief.

Source: Census QuickFacts for Buncombe County.

faqs.q: What rate does Buncombe County charge on 2026 bills?
faqs.a: The county levy is 61.54 cents per $100 of value on the 2021 schedule. Unified Fire District property adds 17.38 cents, and Asheville City Schools adds 11.75 cents.

faqs.q: When do Buncombe bills have to be paid?
faqs.a: September 1 is the usual due date, and no penalty applies through January 5 of the next year. Interest begins January 6.

faqs.q: Is it still possible to protest a Buncombe County value?
faqs.a: The county's August 2026 guidance allowed appeals of the current bill through December 31, 2026, filed at tax.buncombenc.gov or through 828-250-4940. Appeals already made on the 2026 values stay on hold for 2027.

faqs.q: Why is my 2026 Buncombe value unchanged?
faqs.a: A state law pushed the new reappraisal to 2027, so bills use the 2021 values. A change only shows up if you added or altered improvements.

faqs.q: Which Buncombe homeowners qualify for tax relief?
faqs.a: People 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled within the income cap, plus veterans with a permanent and total service-connected disability. Applications run January 1 through June 1, and the exemptions desk is at 828-250-4915.
